nodes.label: hypertension
nodes.desc: An artery disease characterized by chronic elevated blood pressure in the arteries.

nodes.label: essential hypertension
nodes.desc: Xref MGI. OMIM mapping confirmed by DO. [SN]. A hypertension with no known cause. It is the most common type of hypertension.

nodes.label: hypertension and brachydactyly syndrome
nodes.desc: A syndrome characterized by brachydactyly type E, severe salt-independent but age-dependent hypertension, an increased fibroblast growth rate, neurovascular contact at the rostral-ventrolateral medulla, altered baroreflex blood pressure regulation, and increased risk of stroke when untreated that has_material_basis_in heterozygous mutation in PDE3A on 12p12.2.
syn: type E brachydactyly with short stature and hypertension

nodes.label: artery disease
nodes.desc: A vascular disease that is located_in an artery.

nodes.label: vascular disease
nodes.desc: A cardiovascular system disease that primarily affects the blood vessels which includes the arteries, veins and capillaries that carry blood to and from the heart.

nodes.label: arterial calcification of infancy
nodes.desc: Xref MGI. OMIM mapping confirmed by DO. [SN]. A vascular disease that is characterized by generalized calcification of the arterial internal elastic lamina, leading to rupture of the lamina and occlusive changes in the tunica intima with stenosis and decreased elasticity of the vessel wall.

nodes.label: peripheral artery disease
nodes.desc: An artery disease that is characterized by build up of plaque in the arteries that carry blood to your head, organs, and limbs.

nodes.label: retinal arterial tortuosity
nodes.desc: An artery disease characterized by pronounced tortuosity of second- and third-order retinal arteries with normal first-order arteries and venous system that has_material_basis_in heterozygous mutation in the COL4A1 gene on chromosome 13q34.

nodes.label: vertebral artery occlusion
syn: Occlusion and stenosis of vertebral artery

nodes.label: Sneddon syndrome
nodes.desc: An artery disease that is characterized by onset of livedo reticularis in the second decade and onset of cerebrovascular disease in early adulthood and that has_material_basis_in compound heterozygous mutation in the CECR1 gene (ADA2) on chromosome 22q11.
syn: Idiopathic livedo reticularis with systemic involvement

nodes.label: central retinal artery occlusion
nodes.desc: A retinal artery occlusion characterized by blockage of blood flow through the central retinal artery.

nodes.label: arteriosclerosis
nodes.desc: An artery disease that is characterized by a thickening and hardening of arterial walls in the arteries.

nodes.label: Takayasu's arteritis
nodes.desc: OMIM mapping confirmed by DO. [SN]. A vasculitis that involves inflammation of the aorta that carries blood from the heart to the rest of the body.

nodes.label: coronary artery disease
nodes.desc: Xref MGI. An artery disease that is characterized by plaque building up along the inner walls of the arteries of the heart resulting in a narrowing of the arteries and a reduced blood supply to the cardiac muscles.

nodes.label: pre-eclampsia
nodes.desc: Xref MGI. OMIM mapping confirmed by DO. [SN]. A hypertension occurring during pregnancy characterized by large amounts of protein in the urine (proteinuria) and edema, usually by the last trimester of pregnancy.

nodes.label: malignant hypertension
nodes.desc: A hypertension that is characterized by rapid onset of extremely high blood pressure.

nodes.label: pulmonary hypertension
nodes.desc: A hypertension characterized by an increase of blood pressure in the pulmonary artery, pulmonary vein or pulmonary capillaries.

nodes.label: autosomal dominant disease
nodes.desc: An autosomal genetic disease that is characterized by the presence of one disease-associated mutation of a gene which is sufficient to cause the disease.

nodes.label: syndrome
nodes.desc: A disease characterized by a group of signs and symptoms that occur together and characterize a particular abnormality.

nodes.label: autosomal genetic disease
nodes.desc: A monogenic disease that has_material_basis_in a mutation on one of the non-sex chromosomes.

nodes.label: idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis
nodes.desc: OMIM mapping confirmed by DO. [SN]. A pulmonary fibrosis that is characterized by scarring of the lung characterized by stiffness in the lungs and makes it difficult to breathe.

nodes.label: lacrimoauriculodentodigital syndrome 1
nodes.desc: OMIM mapping confirmed by DO. [SN]. A syndrome that has_material_basis_in heterozygous mutation in the tyrosine kinase domain of the FGFR2 gene on chromosome 10q26 and that is characterized by autosomal dominant inheritance of abnormalities affecting the lacrimal and salivary glands and ducts, ears, teeth and fingers and toes.

nodes.label: Hailey-Hailey disease
nodes.desc: OMIM mapping confirmed by DO. [SN]. A pemphigus that is characterized by recurring blistering most commonly occurring in the folds of the skin, particularly the groin and axillary regions, and has_material_basis_in mutations in the ATP2C1 gene that result in loss of adhesion within the skin. Other sites of the body, such as the neck, perianal, and submammary regions, may likewise be affected.

nodes.label: multiple endocrine neoplasia type 2A
nodes.desc: OMIM mapping confirmed by DO. [SN]. A multiple endocrine neoplasia characterized by medullary carcinoma of the thyroid, pheochromocytoma, hyperparathyroidism, and occasionally cutaneous lichen amyloidosis.

nodes.label: Andersen-Tawil syndrome
nodes.desc: OMIM mapping confirmed by DO. [SN]. A long QT syndrome that has_material_basis_in autosomal dominant inheritance of a mutation in the KCNJ2 gene which disrupts the rhythm of the heart's lower chambers (ventricular arrhythmia) and results_in an unusually small lower jaw (micrognathia), low-set ears, and an abnormal curvature of the fingers called clinodactyly.

nodes.label: Frasier syndrome
nodes.desc: OMIM mapping confirmed by DO. [SN]. A syndrome that is characterized by gonadal dysgenesis, streak gonads, progressive focal segmental glomerulonephropathy and the development of urogenital cancers that is the result of mutation in the WT1 gene.

nodes.label: pachyonychia congenita
nodes.desc: OMIM mapping confirmed by DO. [SN]. A syndrome that is characterized by hypertrophic nails and hyperkeratosis of the hands and feet and has_material_basis_in gene mutations that result in changes in keratin.

nodes.label: campomelic dysplasia
nodes.desc: OMIM mapping confirmed by DO. [SN]. An osteochondrodysplasia that has_material_basis_in heterozygous mutation in the SOX9 gene on chromosome 17q24 and that is characterized by congenital shortness and bowing of long tubular bones, especially in the lower extremities, as well as by hypoplastic scapulae, narrow iliac wings, and nonmineralized thoracic pedicles.

nodes.label: Loeys-Dietz syndrome
nodes.desc: Xref MGI. OMIM mapping confirmed by DO. [SN]. A syndrome that is characterized by increased risk of aortic aneurysm and dissection, elongated limbs, hypertelorism, bifid uvula and easy skin bruising due to mutations in TGFB3 that results in connective tissue defects.

nodes.label: Costello syndrome
nodes.desc: OMIM mapping confirmed by DO. [SN]. A RASopathy characterized by craniofacial dysmorphology, cardiac defects, mild mental retardation, and high birth weight followed by a failure to thrive and developmental delays.

nodes.label: Carney complex
nodes.desc: Xref MGI. OMIM mapping confirmed by DO. [SN]. A syndrome characterized by myxomas, spotty pigmentation of the skin and endocrine overactivity.

nodes.label: monilethrix
nodes.desc: OMIM mapping confirmed by DO. [SN]. A hair disease that is characterized by short, easily broken hair that results in alopecia and has_material_basis_in mutations in genes for type II hair cortex keratins.

nodes.label: maturity-onset diabetes of the young
nodes.desc: Xref MGI. OMIM mapping confirmed by DO. [SN]. A diabetes mellitus that has_material_basis_in autosomal dominant inheritance of mutations in the MODY genes impacting beta-cell function, typically occurring before 25 years of age and caused by primary insulin secretion defects.

nodes.label: Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 3
nodes.desc: OMIM mapping confirmed by DO. [SN]. A Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease that is characterized by motor and sensory peripheral neuropathies caused by demyelination.

nodes.label: congenital adrenal insufficiency
nodes.desc: OMIM mapping confirmed by DO. [SN]. An adrenal gland disease that is characterized by cortisol deficiency, hypoaldosteronism and excessive or insufficient sex hormones, has_material_basis_in the mutation in the gene for 21-hydroxylase, 11beta-hydroxylase, 3beta-hydroxysteroid, 17alpha-hydroxylase or 20,22-desmolase.
syn: ADRENAL INSUFFICIENCY, CONGENITAL, WITH 46,XY SEX REVERSAL, PARTIAL OR COMPLETE
Adrenal insufficiency, congenital, with 46,XY sex reversal

nodes.label: type 2 diabetes mellitus
nodes.desc: Xref MGI. OMIM mapping confirmed by DO. [SN]. A diabetes mellitus that is characterized by high blood sugar, insulin resistance, and relative lack of insulin.

nodes.label: type 1 diabetes mellitus 2
nodes.desc: A type 1 diabetes mellitus that has_material_basis_in autosomal dominant inheritance of mutation of the INS gene on chromosome 11p15.5.

nodes.label: type 1 diabetes mellitus 20
nodes.desc: A type 1 diabetes mellitus that has_material_basis_in mutation of the HNF1A gene on chromosome 12q24.31.

nodes.label: diabetes mellitus
nodes.desc: A glucose metabolism disease that is characterized by chronic hyperglycaemia with disturbances of carbohydrate, fat and protein metabolism resulting from defects in insulin secretion, insulin action, or both.

nodes.label: glucose metabolism disease
nodes.desc: A carbohydrate metabolic disorder that is characterized by blood glucose levels which cannot be maintained within the normal range.

nodes.label: gestational diabetes
nodes.desc: A diabetes mellitus that manifests during pregnancy.

nodes.label: neonatal diabetes mellitus
nodes.desc: A diabetes mellitus that is characterized by hyperglycemia occurring within the first 6 months of life.
syn: diabetes mellitus syndrome in newborn infant

nodes.label: type 1 diabetes mellitus
nodes.desc: Xref MGI. OMIM mapping confirmed by DO. [SN]. A diabetes mellitus that is characterized by destruction of pancreatic beta cells resulting in absent or extremely low insulin production.

nodes.label: endocrine system disease
nodes.desc: A disease of anatomical entity that is located_in endocrine glands which secretes a type of hormone directly into the bloodstream to regulate the body.

nodes.label: primary immunodeficiency disease
nodes.desc: Xref MGI. An immune system disease that results when one or more essential parts of the immune system is missing or not working properly at birth due to a genetic mutation.

nodes.label: latent autoimmune diabetes in adults
nodes.desc: A type 1 diabetes mellitus that is characterized by a less intensive autoimmune process, highly variable β-cell destruction, different degrees of insulin resistance and heterogeneous titre and pattern of islet autoantibody, sharing features with both type 1 and type 2 diabetes mellitus.

nodes.label: type 1 diabetes mellitus 3
nodes.desc: A type 1 diabetes mellitus that has_material_basis_in mutation of the locus at chromosome 15q26.

nodes.label: type 1 diabetes mellitus 4
nodes.desc: A type 1 diabetes mellitus that has_material_basis_in mutation of the locus at chromosome 11q13.

nodes.label: type 1 diabetes mellitus 5
nodes.desc: A type 1 diabetes mellitus that has_material_basis_in mutation of the SUMO4 gene on chromosome 6q25.1.

nodes.label: type 1 diabetes mellitus 6
nodes.desc: A type 1 diabetes mellitus that has_material_basis_in mutation of the locus at chromosome 18q21.

nodes.label: type 1 diabetes mellitus 7
nodes.desc: A type 1 diabetes mellitus that has_material_basis_in mutation of the locus at chromosome 2q31.

nodes.label: type 1 diabetes mellitus 8
nodes.desc: A type 1 diabetes mellituss that has_material_basis_in mutation of the locus at chromosome 6q25-q27.

nodes.label: type 1 diabetes mellitus 10
nodes.desc: A type 1 diabetes mellitus that has_material_basis_in mutation of the IL2RA gene on chromosome 10p15.1.

nodes.label: type 1 diabetes mellitus 11
nodes.desc: A type 1 diabetes mellitus that has_material_basis_in mutation of the locus at chromosome 14q24.3-q31.

nodes.label: type 1 diabetes mellitus 12
nodes.desc: A type 1 diabetes mellitus that has_material_basis_in mutation of the CTLA4 gene on chromosome 2q33.2.

nodes.label: type 1 diabetes mellitus 13
nodes.desc: A type 1 diabetes mellituss that has_material_basis_in mutation of the locus at chromosome 2q34.

nodes.label: type 1 diabetes mellitus 15
nodes.desc: A type 1 diabetes mellitus that has_material_basis_in mutation of the locus at chromosome 6q21.

nodes.label: type 1 diabetes mellitus 17
nodes.desc: A type 1 diabetes mellitus that has_material_basis_in mutation of the locus at chromosome 10q25.

nodes.label: type 1 diabetes mellitus 18
nodes.desc: A type 1 diabetes mellitus that has_material_basis_in mutation of the locus at chromosome 5q31.1-q33.1.

nodes.label: asthma
nodes.desc: Xref MGI. A bronchial disease that is characterized by chronic inflammation and narrowing of the airways, which is caused by a combination of environmental and genetic factors. The disease has_symptom recurring periods of wheezing (a whistling sound while breathing), has_symptom chest tightness, has_symptom shortness of breath, has_symptom mucus production and has_symptom coughing.
syn: chronic obstructive asthma with acute exacerbation
chronic obstructive asthma with status asthmaticus

nodes.label: allergic asthma
nodes.desc: An extrinsic asthma that is characterized by symptoms that are triggered by an allergic reaction caused by inhaled allergens such as dust mite allergen, pet dander, pollen and mold. The disease has_symptom coughing, has_symptom wheezing, has_symptom shortness of breath or has_symptom rapid breathing, and has_symptom chest tightness.

nodes.label: status asthmaticus
nodes.desc: An acute asthma that is characterized by an acute episode with a progressive severity that is poorly responsive to standard therapeutic measures, regardless of disease severity or phenotypic variant.

nodes.label: bronchial disease
nodes.desc: A lower respiratory tract disease that affects the airways leading into the lungs, which is caused due to inflammation of the bronchi and bronchioles, infection, or blockage.

nodes.label: lower respiratory tract disease
nodes.desc: A respiratory system disease which involves the lower respiratory tract.

nodes.label: bronchus carcinoma in situ
nodes.desc: An in situ carcinoma located_in the bronchus that most commonly develops into adenocarcinoma.

nodes.label: bronchus cancer
nodes.desc: A respiratory system cancer that is located_in the bronchus.
syn: malignant neoplasm of bronchus and lung
malignant neoplasm of bronchus or lung

nodes.label: bronchiolitis obliterans
nodes.desc: A obstructive lung disease involving obstruction of the bronchioles due to inflammation and fibrosis which occurs as a complication of various lung conditions or physiological insults.

nodes.label: bronchiolitis
nodes.desc: A lung disease that is an inflammation of the bronchioles, the smallest air passages of the lungs. It is caused by viruses and bacteria. The disease has_symptom cough, has_symptom wheezing, has_symptom shortness of breath, has_symptom fever, has_symptom nasal flaring in infants and has_symptom bluish skin due to lack of oxygen.

nodes.label: bronchitis
nodes.desc: A bronchial disease that is an inflammation of the bronchial tubes. It is caused by bacteria and viruses. The disease has_symptom cough with mucus, has_symptom shortness of breath, has_symptom low fever and has_symptom chest tightness.

nodes.label: bronchiectasis
nodes.desc: Xref MGI. OMIM mapping confirmed by DO. [SN]. A bronchial disease that is a chronic inflammatory condition of one or more bronchi or bronchioles marked by dilatation and loss of elasticity of the walls resulting from damage to the airway wall leading to the formation of small sacs on the bronchial wall and impairment of cilia mobility in the lung. Inflammation of the bronchial wall increases mucus secretion which serves as a breeding ground for bacteria. Bronchiectasis is caused by repeated respiratory infections, immune deficiency disorders, hereditary disorders (cystic fibrosis or primary ciliary dyskinesia), mechanical factors (inhaled object or a lung tumor) or inhaling toxic substances.

nodes.label: respiratory allergy
nodes.desc: An allergic disease that is located_in the respiratory tract.

nodes.label: extrinsic asthma
nodes.desc: A chronic asthma that is triggered by an allergen and that is characterized by an immune system overreaction to a harmless substance, such as pollen or dust, with the subsequent release of immunoglobin E (IgE) antibodies.

nodes.label: allergic disease
nodes.desc: An immune system disease that is an exaggerated immune response to allergens, such as insect venom, dust mites, pollen, pet dander, drugs or some foods.

nodes.label: chronic asthma
nodes.desc: An asthma that is characterized by the development of persistent airway inflammation and recurrent attacks of breathlessness and wheezing, which vary in severity and frequency.

nodes.label: remazole black respiratory allergy
nodes.desc: A respiratory allergy that has_allergic_trigger remazole black-GR.

nodes.label: chloramine T respiratory allergy
nodes.desc: A respiratory allergy that has_allergic_trigger chloramine T.

nodes.label: 4-vinylcyclohexene dioxide respiratory allergy
nodes.desc: A respiratory allergy that has_allergic_trigger 4-vinylcyclohexene dioxide.
syn: respiratory allergy to vinyl cyclohexene diepoxide

nodes.label: acid anhydride respiratory allergy
nodes.desc: A respiratory allergy that has_allergic_trigger acid anhydride.

nodes.label: pollen allergy
nodes.desc: A respiratory allergy triggered by pollen.

nodes.label: berylliosis
nodes.desc: A pneumoconiosis that involves allergic response located_in lungs caused by inhalation of beryllium compounds.

nodes.label: allergic bronchopulmonary aspergillosis
nodes.desc: OMIM mapping confirmed by DO. [SN]. An aspergillosis that involves an allergic reaction due to the spores of Aspergillus moulds (A. fumigatus), which colonizes the mucus in the airways causing inflammation. The disease has symptom cough, has symptom wheezing and has symptom fever.

nodes.label: allergic rhinitis
nodes.desc: A rhinitis that is an allergic inflammation and irritation of the nasal airways involving sneezing, runny nose, nasal congestion, itching and tearing of the eyes caused by exposure to an allergen such as pollen, dust, mold, animal dander and droppings of cockroaches or house dust mites.

nodes.label: acute asthma
nodes.desc: An asthma that is characterized by severe and sudden onset of increasing wheezing, airways closing, smooth muscle contraction, mucus plugging and lower airway edema that may be reversible upon treatment.

nodes.label: near-fatal asthma
nodes.desc: An acute asthma that is characterized by a respiratory arrest or arterial carbon dioxide tension greater than 50 mmHg, with or without altered consciousness, requiring mechanical ventilation.

nodes.label: rheumatoid arthritis
nodes.desc: OMIM mapping confirmed by DO. [SN]. An arthritis that is an autoimmune disease which attacks healthy cells and tissue located_in joint.

nodes.label: systemic juvenile rheumatoid arthritis
nodes.desc: Xref MGI. A rheumatoid arthritis that involves an autoimmune disease onset in children under 16 which attacks the healthy cells and tissue of located_in joint.

nodes.label: rheumatoid arthritis interstitial lung disease
nodes.desc: An interstitial lung disease that is characterized by the development of pleuroparenchymal disease secondary to rheumatoid arthritis, including pleural effusions, pleural fibrosis, pulmonary vascular disease, and airway complications.

nodes.label: arthritis
nodes.desc: A bone inflammation disease that involves a response to irritation or injury, characterized by joint pain, swelling, stiffness located_in joint.

nodes.label: immune system disease
nodes.desc: A disease of anatomical entity that is located_in the immune system.

nodes.label: bone inflammation disease
nodes.desc: A bone disease that results_in inflammation of the located_in bone.

nodes.label: autoinflammatory disease
nodes.desc: A primary immunodeficiency disease that is characterized by the activation of innate immune cells without an infection or injury being present, thus kickstarting the release of cytokines and other immune responses, causing fever and inflammation.

nodes.label: immunodeficiency 113
nodes.desc: A primary immunodeficiency disease that is characterized by recurrent infections and usually show features of autoimmunity and autoinflammation, such as hemolytic anemia, thrombocytopenia, hepatosplenomegaly, leukocytosis, neutrophilia, and elevated acute phase reactants, and that has_material_basis_in homozygous mutation in the ARPC5 gene on chromosome 1q25.

nodes.label: WHIM syndrome 1
nodes.desc: An immunodeficiency disease that is characterized by neutropenia, hypogammaglobulinemia, and extensive human papillomavirus infection and that has_material_basis_in heterozygous mutation in the CXCR4 gene on chromosome 2q22.

nodes.label: lymphoproliferative syndrome
nodes.desc: A primary immunodeficiency disease characterized by immune dysregulation typically after viral infection, usually associated with Epstein-Barr viral infection.
syn: Combined immunodeficiency due to ITK deficiency

nodes.label: WHIM syndrome 2
nodes.desc: An immunodeficiency disease that is characterized by chronic neutropenia and myelokathexis, which is impaired neutrophil mobilization from the bone marrow and that has_material_basis_in homozygous mutation in the CXCR2 gene on chromosome 2q35.
syn: WARTS, HYPOGAMMAGLOBULINEMIA, INFECTIONS, AND MYELOKATHEXIS SYNDROME 2

nodes.label: immunodeficiency 80
nodes.desc: A primary immunodeficiency disease that is characterized by variable manifestations and that has_material_basis_in compound heterozygous mutation in the MCM10 gene on chromosome 10p13.
syn: immunodeficiency 80 with or without cautosomal recessive inheritancediomyopathy

nodes.label: immunodeficiency 81
nodes.desc: A primary immunodeficiency disease that is characterized by highly variable phenotype that may include both immunodeficiency with recurrent infections, including bacterial and fungal infections, as well as autoimmune features, including autoimmune hemolytic anemia, pancytopenia, thrombocytopenia, and inflammatory bowel disease and that has_material_basis_in homozygous or compound heterozygous mutation in the SLP76 gene on chromosome 5q33.

nodes.label: immunodeficiency 82
nodes.desc: A primary immunodeficiency disease that is characterized by recurrent infections with various organisms, as well as noninfectious inflammation manifest as lymphocytic organ infiltration with gastritis, colitis, and lung, liver, CNS, or skin disease and and that has_material_basis_in heterozygous mutation in the SYK gene on chromosome 9q22.

nodes.label: immunodeficiency 84
nodes.desc: A primary immunodeficiency disease that is characterized by recurrent sinopulmonary infections from childhood associated with low levels of B cells and impaired early B-cell development and that has_material_basis_in heterozygous mutation in the IKZF3 gene on chromosome 17q12-q21.

nodes.label: immunodeficiency 85
nodes.desc: A primary immunodeficiency disease characterized by onset of atopic eczema and recurrent respiratory infections in the first decade of life that has_material_basis_in heterozygous mutation in the TOM1 gene on chromosome 22q12.

nodes.label: immunodeficiency 88
nodes.desc: A primary immunodeficiency disease that is characterized by the development of disseminated mycobacterial disease following vaccination with BCG and that has_material_basis_in homozygous mutation in the TBX21 gene on chromosome 17q21.

nodes.label: immunodeficiency 89
nodes.desc: A primary immunodeficiency disease that is characterized by adult onset of recurrent infections, allergies, microcytic anemia, and Crohn disease and that has_material_basis_in homozygous mutation in the CARD10 gene on chromosome 22q13.

nodes.label: immunodeficiency 90
nodes.desc: A primary immunodeficiency disease that is characterized by infancy or early childhood with recurrent fevers and bacterial or viral infections associated with central nervous system symptoms, including irritability, drowsiness, variable seizures, and white matter abnormalities on brain imaging and that has_material_basis_in homozygous or compound heterozygous mutation in the FADD gene on chromosome 11q13.
syn: immunodeficiency 90 with encephalopathy, functional hyposplenia, and hepatic dysfunction

nodes.label: immunodeficiency 91
nodes.desc: A primary immunodeficiency disease that is characterized by both immunodeficiency and recurrent infections, often to viruses or mycobacteria, as well as by hyperinflammation with systemic involvement and that has_material_basis_in homozygous or compound heterozygous mutation in the ZNFX1 gene on chromosome 20q13.

nodes.label: immunodeficiency 92
nodes.desc: A primary immunodeficiency disease that is characterized by the onset of recurrent infections in infancy or early childhood and that has_material_basis_in homozygous mutation in the REL gene on chromosome 2p16.

nodes.label: adult-onset Still's disease
nodes.desc: A rheumatoid arthritis that is characterized by high fevers, rash, sore throat and joint pain.

nodes.label: interstitial lung disease
nodes.desc: A lung disease that is characterized by inflammation and altered lung interstitium compromising pulmonary function and often has_symptom shortness of breath, dyspnea, and/or cough.

nodes.label: connective tissue disease
nodes.desc: A musculoskeletal system disease that affects tissues such as skin, tendons, and cartilage.

nodes.label: lung disease
nodes.desc: Updating out dated CUI and removing lung abscess as a synonym. A lower respiratory tract disease in which the function of the lungs is adversely affected by narrowing or blockage of the airways resulting in poor air flow, a loss of elasticity in the lungs that produces a decrease in the total volume of air that the lungs are able to hold, and clotting, scarring, or inflammation of the blood vessels that affect the ability of the lungs to take up oxygen and to release carbon dioxide.

nodes.label: interstitial lung disease 1
nodes.desc: An interstitial lung disease characterized by a progressive remodeling of the alveolar interstitium that has_material_basis_in heterozygous mutation in the SFTPA1 gene on chromosome 10q22.

nodes.label: interstitial lung disease 2
nodes.desc: An interstitial lung disease pulmonary fibrosis that is characterized by scarring of the lung and that has_material_basis_in heterozygous mutation in the SFTPA2 gene on chromosome 10q22.

nodes.label: pneumoconiosis
nodes.desc: An interstitial lung disease that is caused by the inhalation of dust.

nodes.label: pulmonary fibrosis
nodes.desc: An interstitial lung disease that is characterized by destruction, scarring, and thickening of the interstitial lung tissues and progressive pulmonary function loss in a restrictive pattern, has_symptom progressive shortness of breath, fatigue, and chronic cough, possibly has_material_basis_in exposure to certain chemicals, autoimmune conditions, and radiation. It can be caused by inhaling hazardous chemicals, certain diseases, medication and genetics or unknown causes.

nodes.label: extrinsic allergic alveolitis
nodes.desc: An interstitial lung disease involving inflammation of alveoli and smallest airways (bronchioles) of the lung caused by an allergic reaction to inhaled organic dusts containing microorganisms or proteins, and chemicals. Symptoms include chills, cough, fever, malaise, shortness of breath, loss of appetite and weight loss.

nodes.label: breast cancer
nodes.desc: Xref MGI. OMIM mapping confirmed by DO. [SN]. An organ system cancer that originates in the mammary gland.

nodes.label: triple-negative breast cancer
nodes.desc: A breast cancer that is characterized by the absence of estrogen, progresterone and HER2 (EBBR2) receptors.
syn: hormone receptor negative/human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 negative breast cancer
human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 negative/hormone receptor negative breast cancer

nodes.label: hormone receptor-positive/HER2-negative breast cancer
nodes.desc: A HER2 negative breast cancer characterized by at least one of the estrogen or progesterone receptors and the absence of HER2 (EBBR2) protein.
syn: hormone receptor positive/human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 negative breast cancer
human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 negative/hormone receptor positive breast cancer

nodes.label: organ system cancer
nodes.desc: A cancer that is classified based on the organ it starts in.

nodes.label: breast disease
nodes.desc: A disease of anatomical entity that is located_in the breast.

nodes.label: cancer
nodes.desc: Updating out dated UMLS CUI. A disease of cellular proliferation that is malignant and primary, characterized by uncontrolled cellular proliferation, local cell invasion and metastasis.

nodes.label: disease of anatomical entity
nodes.desc: A disease that manifests in a defined anatomical structure.

nodes.label: respiratory system cancer
nodes.desc: An organ system cancer located_in the respiratory system that is characterized by uncontrolled cellular proliferation in the respiratory tract.

nodes.label: immune system cancer
nodes.desc: An organ system cancer located_in the immune system that is characterized by uncontrolled cellular proliferation in organs of the immune system.

nodes.label: musculoskeletal system cancer
nodes.desc: An organ system cancer located_in the muscular and skeletal organs and characterized by uncontrolled cellular proliferation of the musculoskeletal organs.

nodes.label: integumentary system cancer
nodes.desc: An organ system cancer that is located_in the skin, hair and nails.

nodes.label: head and neck cancer
nodes.desc: An organ system cancer that arises in the head or neck region. This region includes the nasal cavity, sinuses, lips, mouth, salivary glands, throat, or larynx.

nodes.label: endocrine gland cancer
nodes.desc: An organ system cancer located_in endocrine system that is characterized by uncontrolled cellular proliferation of the hormone producing glands of the endocrine system.

nodes.label: peritoneum cancer
nodes.desc: An organ system cancer that is located in the peritoneum.

nodes.label: cardiovascular cancer
nodes.desc: An organ system cancer that located_in the heart and blood vessels.

nodes.label: reproductive organ cancer
nodes.desc: An organ system cancer that is manifested in the reproductive organs.

nodes.label: hematologic cancer
nodes.desc: An organ system cancer located in the hematological system that is characterized by uncontrolled cellular proliferation in blood, bone marrow and lymph nodes.

nodes.label: nervous system cancer
nodes.desc: An organ system cancer located_in the nervous system that affects the central or peripheral nervous system.

nodes.label: gastrointestinal system cancer
nodes.desc: An organ system cancer located_in gastrointestinal tract that is manifested in organs of the gastrointestinal system.

nodes.label: urinary system cancer
nodes.desc: An organ system cancer that is located_in the kidneys, ureteres, bladder or urethra.

nodes.label: thoracic cancer
nodes.desc: An organ system cancer located_in the thoracic cavity that develops in the different types of cells within the lungs, as well as less common cancers of the esophagus, the trachea, or the chest wall.

nodes.label: HER2 negative breast cancer
nodes.desc: Absence of HER2 protein is usually represented by an immunohistochemistry (IHC) staining score of 0 with no membrane staining. A breast cancer that is characterized by the absence of HER2 (EBBR2) protein.
syn: human epidermal growth factor 2 negative breast cancer
human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 negative breast cancer

nodes.label: hormone receptor-negative breast cancer
nodes.desc: This term is designed as a grouping term for any hormone receptor-negative breast cancer: estrogen receptor-negative, progesterone receptor-negative, or both. When used by clinicians, 'hormone receptor-negative' generally refers to the latter. For data annotation, use more specific hormone receptor-negative, or hormone receptor-positive, terms than this one whenever possible. A breast cancer characterized by the absence of hormone receptors.

nodes.label: hormone receptor-positive breast cancer
nodes.desc: A breast cancer characterized by the presence of at least one of the estrogen or progesterone receptors.

nodes.label: Ile(5)-angiotensin II
nodes.desc: An angiotensin II that acts on the central nervous system (PDB entry: 1N9V).

nodes.label: riociguat
nodes.desc: A carbamate ester that is the methyl ester of {4,6-diamino-2-[1-(2-fluorobenzyl)-1H-pyrazolo[3,4-b]pyridin-3-yl]pyrimidin-5-yl}methylcarbamic acid. It is used for treatment of chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension and pulmonary arterial hypertension

nodes.label: diltiazem
nodes.desc: A 5-[2-(dimethylamino)ethyl]-2-(4-methoxyphenyl)-4-oxo-2,3,4,5-tetrahydro-1,5-benzothiazepin-3-yl acetate in which both stereocentres have S configuration. A calcium-channel blocker and vasodilator, it is used as the hydrochloride in the management of angina pectoris and hypertension.

nodes.label: fosinoprilat
nodes.desc: A phosphinic acid-containing N-acyl derivative of (4S)-cyclohexyl-L-proline. An inhibitor of angiotensin converting enzyme (ACE), it is used as the phosphinate ester pro-drug fosinopril for treatment of hypertension and chronic heart failure.

nodes.label: Byvalson
nodes.desc: A mixture composed of nebivolol hydrochloride and valsartan (trade name Byvalson) that is used for treatment of hypertension by lowering blood pressure.

nodes.label: nebivolol hydrochloride
nodes.desc: A racemate consisting of equal amounts of (R,S,S,S)- and (S,R,R,R)-nebivolol hydrochloride. A cardioselective beta-blocker, it has vasodilatory activity but lacks intrinsic sympathomimetic and membrane-stabilising activity. It is used as the hydrochloride salt for the management of hypertension, and as an adjunct to standard therapy in elderly patients with stable chronic heart failure.

nodes.label: beraprost
nodes.desc: An organic heterotricyclic compound that is (3aS,8bS)-2,3,3a,8b-tetrahydro-1H-benzo[b]cyclopenta[d]furan in which the hydrogens at positions 1R, 2R and 5 are replaced by (3S)-3-hydroxy-4-methyloct-1-en-6-yn-1-yl, hydroxy and 3-carboxypropyl groups, respectively. It is a prostaglandin receptor agonist which is approved to treat pulmonary arterial hypertension in Asia.

nodes.label: imidaprilat
nodes.desc: A member of the class of imidazolidines that is imidapril in which the ethyl ester group has been hydrolysed to the corresponding acid group. It is the active metabolite of imidapril used to treat hypertension.

nodes.label: forasartan
nodes.desc: A member of the class of pyridines that is pyridine which is substituted at positions 2 and 5 by o-(tetrazol-5-yl)phenyl and (3,5-dibutyl-1,2,4-triazol-1-yl)methyl groups, respectively. It is a nonpeptide antagonist of angiotensin II, type 1 (AT1) receptors, used for the treatment of hypertension.

nodes.label: O-desethyl candesartan
nodes.desc: A benzimidazolecarboxylic acid that is candesartan in which the ethoxy group has been replaced by a hydroxy group. It is the inactive metabolite of the anti-hypertensive drug, candesartan.

nodes.label: cilazapril monohydrate
nodes.desc: A hydrate that is the monohydrate of cilazapril. It is used for the treatment of hypertension and heart failure.

nodes.label: zolasartan
nodes.desc: A member of the class of 1-benzofurans that is 3-bromo-1-benzofuran which is substituted by a 2-(1H-tetrazol-5-yl)phenyl group at position 2 and by a (2-butyl-5-carboxy-4-chloro-1H-imidazol-1-yl)methyl group at position 5. It is an angiotensin II receptor type 1 (AT1) antagonist and was in clinical trials for the treatment of hypertension (now discontinued).

nodes.label: enrasentan
nodes.desc: A member of the class of indanes that is 2,3-dihydro-1H-indene which is substituted by a 1,3-benzodioxol-5-yl group, carboxy group, 2-(2-hydroxyethoxy)-4-methoxyphenyl group and a propoxy group at positions 1S, 2R, 3S and 5, respectively. It is an orally active mixed endothelin A/B receptor antagonist with a 100-fold greater affinity for the endothelin A receptor. The drug was being developed by GSK for the treatment of congestive heart failure and pulmonary hypertension (clinical trials discontinued).

nodes.label: taurine
nodes.desc: An amino sulfonic acid that is the 2-amino derivative of ethanesulfonic acid. It is a naturally occurring amino acid derived from  methionine and cysteine metabolism. An abundant component of fish- and meat-based foods, it has been used as an oral supplement in the treatment of disorders such as cystic fibrosis and hypertension.

nodes.label: pentamethonium
nodes.desc: A quarternary ammonium cation that is cadaverine in which the terminal amino hydrogens are substituted methyl groups. Its bromide and iodide salt exhibits ganglionic blocking activity and used in the treatment of hypertension.

nodes.label: tirzepatide
nodes.desc: A 39-amino acid linear polypeptide which is conjugated to a C20 fatty diacid moiety via a linker connected to lysine-20. It is a dual glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide and glucagon-like peptide-1 agonist used for the management of type 2 diabetes mellitus.

nodes.label: bexagliflozin
nodes.desc: A C-glycosyl comprising of β-D-glucose in which the anomeric hydroxy group is replaced by a 4-chloro-3-({4-[2-(cyclopropyloxy)ethoxy]phenyl}methyl)phenyl group. It is a sodium-glucose co-transporter 2 (SGLT2) inhibitor indicated as an adjunct to diet and exercise to improve glycemic control in adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus.

nodes.label: sotagliflozin
nodes.desc: An S-glycosyl compound that is 1-thio-β-L-xylopyranose in which the anomeric hydroxy group is replaced by a 4-chloro-3-[(4-ethoxyphenyl)methyl]phenyl group and the thiol is replaced by a methylsulfanediyl group. It is an inhibitor of SGLT1 and SGLT2 that is approved to reduce the risk of cardiovascular death, hospitalization for heart failure, and urgent heart failure visit in adults with heart failure or type 2 diabetes mellitus, chronic kidney disease, and other cardiovascular risk.

nodes.label: nateglinide
nodes.desc: An N-acyl-D-phenylalanine resulting from the formal condensation of the amino group of D-phenylalanine with the carboxy group of trans-4-isopropylcyclohexanecarboxylic acid. An orally-administered, rapidly-absorbed, short-acting insulinotropic agent, it is used for the treatment of type 2 diabetes mellitus.

nodes.label: glipizide
nodes.desc: An N-sulfonylurea that is glyburide in which the (5-chloro-2-methoxybenzoyl group is replaced by a (5-methylpyrazin-2-yl)carbonyl group. An oral hypoglycemic agent, it is used in the treatment of type 2 diabetes mellitus.

nodes.label: liraglutide
nodes.desc: A lipopeptide that is an analogue of human GLP-1 in which the lysine residue at position 27 is replaced by arginine and a hexadecanoyl group attached to the remaining lysine via a glutamic acid spacer. Used as an adjunct to diet and exercise to improve glycemic control in adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus.

nodes.label: N-sulfonylurea
nodes.desc: A urea in which one of the hydrogens attached to a nitrogen of the urea group is replaced by a sulfonyl group. The N-sulfonylurea moiety is a key group in various herbicides, as well as in a number of antidiabetic drugs used in the management of type 2 diabetis mellitus.

nodes.label: empagliflozin
nodes.desc: A C-glycosyl compound consisting of a β-glucosyl residue having a (4-chloro-3-{4-[(3S)-tetrahydrofuran-3-yloxy]benzyl}phenyl group at the anomeric centre. A sodium-glucose co-transporter 2 inhibitor used as an adjunct to diet and exercise to improve glycemic control in adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus.

nodes.label: tolazamide
nodes.desc: An N-sulfonylurea that is 1-tosylurea in which a hydrogen attached to the nitrogen at position 3 is replaced by an azepan-1-yl group. A hypoglycemic agent, it is used for the treatment of type 2 diabetes mellitus.

nodes.label: dorzagliatin
nodes.desc: A secondary carboxamide resulting from the formal condensation of the carboxy group of (2S)-2-[4-(2-chlorophenoxy)-2-oxo-2,5-dihydro-1H-pyrrol-1-yl]-4-methylpentanoic acid with the amino group of (2R)-3-(3-amino-1H-pyrrol-1-yl)propane-1,2-diol. It is an allosteric glucokinase activator developed by Hua Medicine for the treatment of type 1 and 2 diabetes mellitus , and diabetic kidney disease.

nodes.label: chlorpropamide
nodes.desc: An N-sulfonylurea that is urea in which a hydrogen attached to one of the nitrogens is substituted by 4-chlorobenzenesulfonyl group and a hydrogen attached to the other nitrogen is substituted by propyl group. Chlorpropamide is a hypoglycaemic agent used in the treatment of type 2 (non-insulin-dependent) diabetes mellitus not responding to dietary modification.

nodes.label: (R)-lisofylline
nodes.desc: A 1-(5-hydroxyhexyl)-3,7-dimethyl-3,7-dihydro-1H-purine-2,6-dione that has (R)-configuration. A synthetic small molecule which was under development for the treatment of type 1 diabetes mellitus.

nodes.label: anti-asthmatic drug
nodes.desc: A drug used to treat asthma.

nodes.label: anti-asthmatic agent
nodes.desc: Any compound that has anti-asthmatic effects.

nodes.label: GSK-256066
nodes.desc: Gsk256066 has been used in trials studying the treatment and diagnostic of SAR, Asthma, Mild Asthma, Allergic Rhinitis, and Seasonal Allergic Rhinitis, among others.

nodes.label: zileuton
nodes.desc: A member of the class of 1-benzothiophenes that is 1-benzothiophene in which the hydrogen at position 2 is replaced by a 1-[carbamoyl(hydroxy)amino]ethyl group. A selective 5-lipoxygenase inhibitor, it inhibits the formation of leukotrienes LTB4, LTC4, LDT4, and LTE4. It is used for the management of chronic asthma.

nodes.label: enprofylline
nodes.desc: Xanthine bearing a propyl substituent at position 3. A bronchodilator, it is used for the symptomatic treatment of asthma and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, and in the management of cerebrovascular insufficiency, sickle cell disease, and diabetic neuropathy.

nodes.label: cinalukast
nodes.desc: 2,2-Diethylsuccinanilic acid substituted at a meta- position by an (E)-2-(4-cyclobutyl-1,3-thiazol-2-yl)ethenyl group. It selectively antagonizes leukotriene D4 at the cysteinyl leukotriene receptor, in the human airway, preventing airway edema, smooth muscle contraction, and enhanced secretion of thick, viscous mucus. It is used in the treatment of asthma.

nodes.label: methylprednisolone suleptanate
nodes.desc: An organic sodium salt that is the monosodium salt of methylprednisolone 21-suleptanic acid ester. It is a prodrug of methylprednisolone developed by Pharmacia Corp for the treatment of asthma.

nodes.label: abediterol
nodes.desc: A quinolone that is 8-hydroxyquinolin-2(1H)-one which carries a 2-{[6-(2,2-difluoro-2-phenylethoxy)hexyl]amino}-1-hydroxyethyl group at position 5. It is a long acting β2-adrenoceptor agonist currently in development for the treatment of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and asthma.

nodes.label: flutropium
nodes.desc: A carboxylic ester resulting from the formal condensation of the carboxy group of hydroxy(diphenyl)acetic acid with the hydroxy group of (3-endo,8-syn)-8-(2-fluoroethyl)-3-hydroxy-8-methyl-8-azoniabicyclo[3.2.1]octane. Its bromide salt is used as a drug for the treatment asthma and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease.

nodes.label: albuterol
nodes.desc: A member of the class of phenylethanolamines that is 4-(2-amino-1-hydroxyethyl)-2-(hydroxymethyl)phenol having a tert-butyl group attached to the nirogen atom. It acts as a β-adrenergic agonist used in the treatment of asthma and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD).

nodes.label: bitolterol
nodes.desc: The di-4-toluate ester of (±)-N-tert-butylnoradrenaline (colterol). A pro-drug for colterol, a β2-adrenergic receptor agonist, bitolterol is used as its methanesulfonate salt for relief of bronchospasm in conditions such as asthma, chronic bronchitis and emphysema.

nodes.label: bitolterol mesylate
nodes.desc: The methanesulfonate salt of bitolterol. A β<small><sub>2</sub></small>-adrenergic receptor agonist, it is used for relief of bronchospasm in conditions such as asthma, chronic bronchitis and emphysema.

nodes.label: fluticasone propionate
nodes.desc: A trifluorinated corticosteroid that consists of 6α,9-difluoro-11β,17α-dihydroxy-17β-{[(fluoromethyl)sulfanyl]carbonyl}-16-methyl-3-oxoandrosta-1,4-diene bearing a propionyl substituent at position 17; has anti-inflammatory, anti-asthmatic and anti-allergic activity.

nodes.label: flutropium bromide
nodes.desc: The organic bromide salt of flutropium. It is used in Japan for the treatment asthma and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease.

nodes.label: Anakinra
nodes.desc: Anakinra is a recombinant human interleukin-1 (IL-1) receptor antagonist (IL-1Ra) composed of 153 amino acid residues. Unlike native human IL-1Ra, anakinra has an additional methionine residue at the amino terminus. This drug binds to the IL-1 receptor, competing with and inhibiting the activity of IL-1 alpha and beta. Anakinra is indicated for the management of rheumatoid arthritis (RA) in patients 18 years of age or older who have failed one or more disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs (DMARDs), as well as the treatment of neonatal-onset multisystem inflammatory disease (NOMID) and deficiency of interleukin-1 receptor antagonist (DIRA). Since IL-1 has an important role in inflammation and immunological responses, anakinra is also used for the off-label treatment of inflammatory diseases. Anakinra is produced using the E. Coli bacterial expression system. On November 14, 2001, it was approved by the FDA for the treatment of rheumatoid arthritis. It was later approved for the treatment of NOMID and DIRA on December 21, 2012, and December 18, 2020, respectively. A few studies have evaluated the use of anakinra for the treatment of coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19). On November 8, 2022, the FDA issued an emergency use authorization (EUA) of anakinra for the treatment of COVID-19 in hospitalized patients who are at risk of progressing to severe respiratory failure. (DrugBank)

nodes.label: auranofin
nodes.desc: An S-glycosyl compound consisting of 2,3,4,6-tetra-O-acetyl-1-thio-β-D-glucopyranose with the sufur atom coordinated to (triethylphosphoranylidene)gold. It is administered orally for the treatment of active progressive rheumatoid arthritis.

nodes.label: aceclofenac
nodes.desc: A monocarboxylic acid that is the carboxymethyl ester of diclofenac. A non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drug related to diclofenac, it is used in the management of osteoarthritis, rheumatoid arthritis, and ankylosing spondylitis.

nodes.label: acemetacin
nodes.desc: A carboxylic ester that is the carboxymethyl ester of indometacin. A non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drug, it is used in the treatment of rheumatoid arthritis, osteoarthritis, and low back pain, as well as for postoperative pain and inflammation. Its activity is due to both acemetacin and its major metabolite, indometacin.

nodes.label: ampiroxicam
nodes.desc: A benzothiazine that is the 1-[(ethoxycarbonyl)oxy]ethyl ether of piroxicam. A prodrug for piroxicam, it is used for the relief of pain and inflammation in musculoskeletal disorders such as rheumatoid arthritis and osteoarthritis.

nodes.label: tenoxicam
nodes.desc: A thienothiazine-derived monocarboxylic acid amide obtained by formal condensation of the carboxy group of 4-hydroxy-2-methylthieno[2,3-e][1,2]thiazine-3-carboxylic acid 1,1-dioxide with the amino group of 2-aminopyridine. Used for the treatment of pain and inflammation in osteoarthritis and rheumatoid arthritis. It is also indicated for short term treatment of acute musculoskeletal disorders including strains, sprains and other soft-tissue injuries.

nodes.label: antirheumatic drug
nodes.desc: A drug used to treat rheumatoid arthritis.

nodes.label: chloroquine
nodes.desc: An aminoquinoline that is quinoline which is substituted at position 4 by a [5-(diethylamino)pentan-2-yl]amino group at at position 7 by chlorine. It is used for the treatment of malaria, hepatic amoebiasis, lupus erythematosus, light-sensitive skin eruptions, and rheumatoid arthritis.

nodes.label: doramapimod
nodes.desc: A member of the class of pyrazoles that is an immunomodulator used for treatment of rheumatoid arthritis, Crohn's disease and psoriasis.

nodes.label: (5Z)-5-(quinoxalin-6-ylmethylidene)-1,3-thiazolidine-2,4-dione
nodes.desc: A quinoxaline derivative  that is quinoxaline in which the hydrogen at position 6 is replaced by a (2,4-dioxo-1,3-thiazolidin-5-ylidene)methyl group. It is a potent inhibitor of the PI3Kγ, with an IC<small><sub>50</sub></small> of 8 nM and inhibits the progression of joint inflammation and damage in both lymphocyte-independent and dependent mouse models of rheumatoid arthritis.

nodes.label: etodolac
nodes.desc: A monocarboxylic acid that is acetic acid in which one of the methyl hydrogens is substituted by a 1,8-diethyl-1,3,4,9-tetrahydropyrano[3,4-b]indol-1-yl moiety. A preferential inhibitor of cyclo-oxygenase 2 and non-steroidal anti-inflammatory, it is used for the treatment of rheumatoid arthritis and osteoarthritis, and for the alleviation of postoperative pain. Administered as the racemate, only the (S)-enantiomer is active.

nodes.label: indometacin
nodes.desc: A member of the class of indole-3-acetic acids that is indole-3-acetic acid in which the indole ring is substituted at positions 1, 2 and 5 by p-chlorobenzoyl, methyl, and methoxy groups, respectively. A non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drug, it is used in the treatment of musculoskeletal and joint disorders including osteoarthritis, rheumatoid arthritis, gout, bursitis and tendinitis.

nodes.label: sodium aurothiomalate
nodes.desc: A variable mixture of the mono- and di-sodium salts of aurothiomalic acid. It is used for treatment of rheumatoid arthritis.

nodes.label: hydroxychloroquine
nodes.desc: An aminoquinoline that is chloroquine in which one of the N-ethyl groups is hydroxylated at position 2. An antimalarial with properties similar to chloroquine that acts against erythrocytic forms of malarial parasites, it is mainly used as the sulfate salt for the treatment of lupus erythematosus, rheumatoid arthritis, and light-sensitive skin eruptions.

nodes.label: (R)-etodolac
nodes.desc: The R-enantiomer of etodolac. It is inactive, in contrast to the enantiomer, (S)-etodolac, which is a preferential inhibitor of cyclo-oxygenase 2 and a non-steroidal anti-inflammatory. The racemate is commonly used for the treatment of rheumatoid arthritis and osteoarthritis, and for the alleviation of postoperative pain.

nodes.label: breast cancer resistance protein inhibitor
nodes.desc: Any inhibitor of breast cancer resistance protein (ABCG2).

nodes.label: gemcitabine
nodes.desc: A 2'-deoxycytidine having geminal fluoro substituents in the 2'-position. An inhibitor of ribonucleotide reductase, gemcitabine is used in the treatment of various carcinomas, particularly non-small cell lung cancer, pancreatic cancer, bladder cancer and breast cancer.

nodes.label: gemcitabine hydrochloride
nodes.desc: A 2'-deoxycytidine hydrochloriode having geminal fluoro substituents in the 2'-position. An inhibitor of ribonucleotide reductase, gemcitabine hydrochloride is used in the treatment of various carcinomas, including non-small cell lung cancer, pancreatic cancer, bladder cancer and breast cancer.

nodes.label: hedychilactone D
nodes.desc: A labdane diterpenoid that is 7,11,13-labdatrien-16,15-olide substituted by a hydroxy group at position 7 and an oxo group at position 6. Isolated from the rhizomes of Hedychium spicatum, it exhibits cytotoxicity against the Colo-205 (Colo-cancer), A-431 (skin cancer), MCF-7 (breast cancer), A-549 (lung cancer) and Chinese hamster ovary cells (CHO).

nodes.label: 9-hydroxy hedychenone
nodes.desc: A labdane diterpenoid that is 15,16-epoxy-7,11,13(16)14-labdatetraen-6-one substituted by a hydroxy group at position 9. Isolated from the rhizomes of Hedychium spicatum, it exhibits cytotoxicity against the Colo-205 (Colo-cancer), A-431 (skin cancer), MCF-7 (breast cancer), A-549 (lung cancer) and Chinese hamster ovary cells (CHO).

nodes.label: oviedomycin
nodes.desc: A member of the class of tetraphenes that is 1,4,7,12-tetrahydrotetraphene substituted by oxo groups at positions 1, 4, 7, and 12, by hydroxy groups at positions 2, 6 and 8, and by a methyl group at position 3. It is a natural product found in Streptomyces antibioticus ATCC 11891 which exhibits cytotoxicity against A549 human lung cancer cells, HepG2 liver cancer cells, and MCF-7 breast cancer cells.

nodes.label: moromycin A
nodes.desc: An angucycline antibiotic that consists of a tetrangomycin skeleton linked to deoxy sugars through C-glycosidic and O-glycosidic bonds at positions 9 and 3 respectively. It is isolated from Streptomyces sp.KY002 and exhibits cytotoxicity against human lung cancer and MCF-7 human breast cancer cells.

nodes.label: moromycin B
nodes.desc: An angucycline that consists of tetrangomycin linked to a deoxy sugar moiety at position 9 via a C-glycosidic bond. It is isolated from Streptomyces sp.KY002 and exhibits cytotoxicity against human lung cancer and MCF-7 human breast cancer cells.

nodes.label: CX-5461
nodes.desc: An organic heterotetracyclic compound that is 5-oxo-5H-[1,3]benzothiazolo[3,2-a][1,8]naphthyridine-6-carboxylic acid substituted by a 4-methyl-1,4-diazepan-1-yl group at position 2 and in which the carboxy group at position 6 is substituted by a [(5-methylpyrazin-2-yl)methyl]nitrilo group. An inhibitor of ribosomal RNA (rRNA) synthesis which specifically inhibits RNA polymerase I-driven transcription of rRNA in several cancer cell lines. It is currently in phase I/II clinical trials for advanced hematologic malignancies and triple-negative breast cancer with BRCA1/2 mutation.

nodes.label: lobaplatin
nodes.desc: A 1:1 diastereomeric mixture comprising of R,R,S and S,S,S configuration of platinum(II) complexes with 1,2-bis(aminomethyl)cyclobutane as the carrier ligand and lactate as the leaving group. It is a third-generation platinum anticancer drug approved in China for the treatment of chronic myelogenous leukaemia, inoperable metastatic breast cancer and small cell lung cancer.

nodes.label: elacestrant
nodes.desc: A member of the class of tetralins that is 1,2,3,4-tetrahydronaphthalene which is substituted by hydroxy group at position 2 and by a 2-(ethyl{4-[2-(ethylamino)ethyl]benzyl}amino)-4-methoxyphenyl group at position 6R. It is a is an estrogen receptor degrader indicated for the treatment of postmenopausal women or adult men, with ER-positive, HER2-negative, ESR1-mutated advanced or metastatic breast cancer with disease progression following at least one line of endocrine therapy.

nodes.label: capivasertib
nodes.desc: An aminopiperidine that is piperidine substituted by 7H-pyrrolo[2,3-d]pyrimidin-4-yl, amino, and [(1S)-1-(4-chlorophenyl)-3-hydroxypropyl]aminocarbonyl groups at positions 1, 4, and 4, respectively. It is a pan-AKT kinase inhibitor used in combination with fulvestrant for the treatment of adult patients with hormone receptor (HR)-positive, human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2)-negative, locally advanced or metastatic breast cancer with one or more PIK3CA/AKT1/PTEN-alterations.

nodes.label: talazoparib
nodes.desc: Talazoparib is an orally available small molecule inhibitor of the DNA repair enzyme poly ADP-ribose polymerase (PARP) which is used as an antineoplastic agent in the treatment of selected cases of breast cancer. Talazoparib is associated with a moderate rate of serum aminotransferase elevations during therapy and is suspected to cause rare instances of clinically apparent acute liver injury.

nodes.label: vincristine
nodes.desc: A vinca alkaloid with formula C46H56N4O10 found in the Madagascar periwinkle, Catharanthus roseus. It is used (commonly as the corresponding sulfate salt)as a chemotherapy drug for the treatment of leukaemia, lymphoma, myeloma, breast cancer and head and neck cancer.

nodes.label: fulvestrant
nodes.desc: A 3-hydroxy steroid that is 17β-estradiol in which the 7α hydrogen has been replaced by a nonyl group in which one of the hydrogens of the terminal methyl has been replaced by a (4,4,5,5,5-pentafluoropentyl)sulfinyl group. An estrogen receptor antagonist, it is used in the treatment of breast cancer.

nodes.label: carbamate ester
nodes.desc: Any ester of carbamic acid or its N-substituted derivatives.

nodes.label: organofluorine compound
nodes.desc: An organofluorine compound is a compound containing at least one carbon-fluorine bond.

nodes.label: aminopyrimidine
nodes.desc: A member of the class of  pyrimidines that is pyrimidine substituted by at least one amino group and its derivatives.

nodes.label: carboxylic ester
nodes.desc: An ester of a carboxylic acid, R<small><sup>1</small></sup>C(=O)OR<small><sup>2</small></sup>, where R<small><sup>1</small></sup> = H or organyl and R<small><sup>2</small></sup> = organyl.

nodes.label: organohalogen compound
nodes.desc: A compound containing at least one carbon-halogen bond (where X is a halogen atom).

nodes.label: aromatic amine
nodes.desc: An amino compound in which the amino group is linked directly to an aromatic system.

nodes.label: pyrimidines
nodes.desc: Any compound having a pyrimidine as part of its structure.

nodes.label: organonitrogen heterocyclic compound
nodes.desc: Any organonitrogen compound containing a cyclic component with nitrogen and at least one other element as ring member atoms.

nodes.label: 5-[2-(dimethylamino)ethyl]-2-(4-methoxyphenyl)-4-oxo-2,3,4,5-tetrahydro-1,5-benzothiazepin-3-yl acetate
nodes.desc: A lactam that is 2,3-dihydro-1,5-benzothiazepin-4(5H)-one in which positions 2 and 3 are substituted by 4-methoxyphenyl and acetoxy, respectively, while the hydrogen attached to the nitrogen is substituted by a 2-(dimethylamino)ethyl group.

nodes.label: lactam
nodes.desc: Cyclic amides of amino carboxylic acids, having a 1-azacycloalkan-2-one structure, or analogues having unsaturation or heteroatoms replacing one or more carbon atoms of the ring.

nodes.label: aromatic ether
nodes.desc: Any ether in which the oxygen is attached to at least one aryl substituent.

nodes.label: acetate ester
nodes.desc: Any carboxylic ester where the carboxylic acid component is acetic acid.

nodes.label: tertiary amino compound
nodes.desc: A compound formally derived from ammonia by replacing three hydrogen atoms by organyl groups.

nodes.label: phosphinic acids
nodes.desc: H<small><sub>2</sub></small>P(=O)OH  (phosphinic acid) and its P-hydrocarbyl derivatives.

nodes.label: L-proline derivative
nodes.desc: A proteinogenic amino acid derivative resulting from reaction of <small>L</small>-proline at the amino group or the carboxy group, or from the replacement of any hydrogen of <small>L</small>-proline  by a heteroatom.

nodes.label: proline derivative
nodes.desc: An amino acid derivative resulting from reaction of proline at the amino group or the carboxy group, or from the replacement of any hydrogen of proline by a heteroatom. The definition normally excludes peptides containing proline residues.

nodes.label: proteinogenic amino acid derivative
nodes.desc: Any derivative of a proteinogenic amino acid resulting from reaction at an amino group, carboxy group, or a side-chain functional group, or from the replacement of any hydrogen by a heteroatom.

nodes.label: mixture
nodes.desc: A mixture is a chemical substance composed of multiple molecules, at least two of which are of a different kind.

nodes.label: racemate
nodes.desc: A racemate is an equimolar mixture of a pair of enantiomers.

nodes.label: secondary allylic alcohol
nodes.desc: An allylic alcohol in which the carbon atom that links the double bond to the hydroxy group is also attached to one other carbon and one hydrogen.

nodes.label: monocarboxylic acid
nodes.desc: An oxoacid containing a single carboxy group.

nodes.label: organic heterotricyclic compound
nodes.desc: An organic tricyclic compound in which at least one of the rings of the tricyclic skeleton contains one or more heteroatoms.

nodes.label: secondary alcohol
nodes.desc: A secondary alcohol is a compound in which a hydroxy group, ‒OH, is attached to a saturated carbon atom which has two other carbon atoms attached to it.

nodes.label: enyne
nodes.desc: An  acetylenic and an olefinic  compound containing a carbon chain that contains a carbon-carbon double bond and a carbon-carbon triple bond.

nodes.label: allylic alcohol
nodes.desc: An alcohol where the hydroxy group is attached to a saturated carbon atom adjacent to a double bond (R groups may be H, organyl, etc.).

nodes.label: carboxylic acid
nodes.desc: A carbon oxoacid acid carrying at least one ‒C(=O)OH group and having the structure RC(=O)OH, where R is any any monovalent functional group. Carboxylic acids are the most common type of organic acid.

nodes.label: alcohol
nodes.desc: A compound in which a hydroxy group, ‒OH, is attached to a saturated carbon atom.

nodes.label: acetylenic compound
nodes.desc: Any organic molecule containing a C≡C bond.

nodes.label: olefinic compound
nodes.desc: Any organic molecular entity that contains at least one C=C bond.

nodes.label: dicarboxylic acid
nodes.desc: Any carboxylic acid containing two carboxy groups.

nodes.label: dipeptide
nodes.desc: Any molecule that contains two amino-acid residues connected by peptide linkages.

nodes.label: secondary amino compound
nodes.desc: A compound formally derived from ammonia by replacing two hydrogen atoms by organyl groups.

nodes.label: N-acylurea
nodes.desc: A member of the class of ureas that has the general formula R-CO-NH-CO-NH<small><sub>2</sub></small> or R-CO-NH-CO-NH-CO-R', formally derived by the acylation of one or both of the nitrogens of a urea moiety.

nodes.label: dicarboxylic acids and O-substituted derivatives
nodes.desc: A class of carbonyl compound encompassing dicarboxylic acids and any derivatives obtained by substitution of either one or both of the carboxy hydrogens.

nodes.label: oligopeptide
nodes.desc: A peptide containing a relatively small number of amino acids.

nodes.label: organic amino compound
nodes.desc: A compound formally derived from ammonia by replacing one, two or three hydrogen atoms by organyl groups.

nodes.label: benzenes
nodes.desc: Any benzenoid aromatic compound consisting of the benzene skeleton and its substituted derivatives.

nodes.label: pyridines
nodes.desc: Any organonitrogen heterocyclic compound based on a pyridine skeleton and its substituted derivatives.

nodes.label: tetrazoles
nodes.desc: An azole in which the five-membered heterocyclic aromatic skeleton contains four N atoms and one C atom.

nodes.label: triazoles
nodes.desc: An azole in which the five-membered heterocyclic aromatic skeleton contains three N atoms and two C atoms.

nodes.label: azole
nodes.desc: Any monocyclic heteroarene consisting of a five-membered ring containing nitrogen. Azoles can also contain one or more other non-carbon atoms, such as nitrogen, sulfur or oxygen.

nodes.label: benzimidazolecarboxylic acid
nodes.desc: A member of the class of  benzimidazoles carrying a carboxy group at unspecified position.

nodes.label: biphenylyltetrazole
nodes.desc: A member of the class of biphenyls that consists of a biphenyl ring system substituted by a tetrazole ring at an unspecified position.

nodes.label: benzimidazoles
nodes.desc: An organic heterocyclic compound containing a benzene ring fused to an imidazole ring.

nodes.label: biphenyls
nodes.desc: Benzenoid aromatic compounds containing two phenyl or substituted-phenyl groups which are joined together by a single bond.

nodes.label: hydrate
nodes.desc: An addition compound that contains water in weak chemical combination with another compound.

nodes.label: addition compound
nodes.desc: An addition compound contains two or more simpler compounds that can be packed in a definite ratio into a crystal. The term covers donor-acceptor complexes (adducts) and a variety of lattice compounds.

nodes.label: organochlorine compound
nodes.desc: An organochlorine compound is a compound containing at least one carbon-chlorine bond.

nodes.label: organobromine compound
nodes.desc: A compound containing at least one carbon-bromine bond.

nodes.label: imidazolyl carboxylic acid
nodes.desc: Any member of the class of imidazoles in which the imidazole ring is substituted by one (or more) carboxy group(s).

nodes.label: 1-benzofurans
nodes.desc: A member of the class of benzofurans consisting of a 1-benzofuran skeleton and its substituted derivatives thereof.

nodes.label: biaryl
nodes.desc: An organic aromatic compound whose structure contains two aromatic rings or ring systems, joined to each other by a single bond.

nodes.label: chlorine molecular entity
nodes.desc: A halogen molecular entity containing one or more atoms of chlorine.

nodes.label: imidazoles
nodes.desc: A five-membered organic heterocycle containing two nitrogen atoms at positions 1 and 3, or any of its derivatives; compounds containing an imidazole skeleton.

nodes.label: aromatic carboxylic acid
nodes.desc: Any carboxylic acid in which the carboxy group is directly bonded to an aromatic ring.

nodes.label: primary alcohol
nodes.desc: A primary alcohol is a compound in which a hydroxy group, ‒OH, is attached to a saturated carbon atom which has either three hydrogen atoms attached to it or only one other carbon atom and two hydrogen atoms attached to it.

nodes.label: monomethoxybenzene
nodes.desc: Compounds containing a benzene skeleton substituted with one methoxy group.

nodes.label: methoxybenzenes
nodes.desc: Any aromatic ether that consists of a benzene skeleton substituted with one or more methoxy groups.

nodes.label: ether
nodes.desc: An organooxygen compound with formula ROR, where R is not hydrogen.

nodes.label: oxacycle
nodes.desc: Any organic heterocyclic compound containing at least one ring oxygen atom.

nodes.label: carbobicyclic compound
nodes.desc: A bicyclic compound in which all the ring atoms are carbon.

nodes.label: amino sulfonic acid
nodes.desc: An organosulfonic acid containing one or more amino groups.

nodes.label: organosulfonic acid
nodes.desc: An organic derivative of sulfonic acid in which the sulfo group is linked directly to carbon.

nodes.label: quaternary ammonium ion
nodes.desc: A derivative of ammonium, NH<small><sub>4</sub></small><small><sup>+</small></sup>, in which all four of the hydrogens bonded to nitrogen have been replaced with univalent (usually organyl) groups.

nodes.label: organic cation
nodes.desc: Any organic ion with a net positive charge.

nodes.label: ammonium ion derivative
nodes.desc: A derivative of ammonium, NH<small><sub>4</sub></small><small><sup>+</small></sup>, in which one (or more) of the hydrogens bonded to the nitrogen have been replaced with univalent organyl groups. The substituting carbon of the organyl group must not itself be directly attached to a heteroatom (thereby excluding protonated amides, hemiaminals, etc).

nodes.label: polypeptide
nodes.desc: A peptide containing ten or more amino acid residues.

nodes.label: peptide
nodes.desc: Amide derived from two or more amino carboxylic acid molecules (the same or different) by formation of a covalent bond from the carbonyl carbon of one to the nitrogen atom of another with formal loss of water. The term is usually applied to structures formed from α-amino acids, but it includes those derived from any amino carboxylic acid. X = OH, OR, NH2, NHR, etc.

nodes.label: macromolecule
nodes.desc: A macromolecule is a molecule of high relative molecular mass, the structure of which essentially comprises the multiple repetition of units derived, actually or conceptually, from molecules of low relative molecular mass.

nodes.label: C-glycosyl compound
nodes.desc: A glycosyl compound arising formally from the elimination of water from a glycosidic hydroxy group and an H atom bound to a carbon atom, thus creating a C-C bond.

nodes.label: diether
nodes.desc: A polyether in which the number of ether linkages is 2.

nodes.label: cyclopropanes
nodes.desc: Cyclopropane and its derivatives formed by substitution.

nodes.label: monochlorobenzenes
nodes.desc: Any member of the class of chlorobenzenes containing a mono- or poly-substituted benzene ring in which only one substituent is chlorine.

nodes.label: glycosyl compound
nodes.desc: A carbohydrate derivative arising formally from the elimination of water from a glycosidic hydroxy group and an H atom bound to an oxygen, carbon, nitrogen or sulfur atom of a separate entity.

nodes.label: carbohydrate derivative
nodes.desc: Any organooxygen compound derived from a carbohydrate by replacement of one or more hydroxy group(s) by an amino group, a thiol group or similar heteroatomic groups. The term also includes derivatives of these compounds.

nodes.label: polyether
nodes.desc: Any ether that contains more than one ether linkage.

nodes.label: carbocyclic compound
nodes.desc: A homocyclic compound in which all of the ring members are carbon atoms.

nodes.label: chlorobenzenes
nodes.desc: Any organochlorine compound containing a benzene ring which is substituted by one or more chlorines.

nodes.label: S-glycosyl compound
nodes.desc: A glycosyl compound arising formally from the elimination of water from a glycosidic hydroxy group and a S atom bound to a carbon atom, thus creating a C-S bond.

nodes.label: monothioacetal
nodes.desc: A thioacetal having the structure R<small><sub>2</sub></small>C(OR')(SR'). The term includes monothioketals, R ≠ H, as a subclass.

nodes.label: thiosugar
nodes.desc: A carbohydrate derivative in which one or more of the oxygens or hydroxy groups of the parent carbohydrate is replaced by sulfur or -SR, where R can be hydrogen or any group.

nodes.label: N-acyl-D-phenylalanine
nodes.desc: Any N-acyl-D-amino acid obtained by the formal N-acylation of D-phenylalanine.

nodes.label: N-acyl-D-amino acid
nodes.desc: Any N-acyl-amino acid in which the amino acid moiety has D configuration.

nodes.label: monocarboxylic acid amide
nodes.desc: A carboxamide derived from a monocarboxylic acid.

nodes.label: aromatic amide
nodes.desc: An amide in which the amide linkage is bonded directly to an aromatic system.

nodes.label: carboxamide
nodes.desc: An amide of a carboxylic acid, having the structure RC(=O)NR<small><sub>2</sub></small>. The term is used as a suffix in systematic name formation to denote the ‒C(=O)NH<small><sub>2</sub></small> group including its carbon atom.

nodes.label: diazines
nodes.desc: Any organic heterocyclic compound containing a benzene ring in which two of the C-H fragments have been replaced by isolobal nitrogens (the diazine parent structure).

nodes.label: amide
nodes.desc: An amide is a derivative of an oxoacid RkE(=O)l(OH)m (l ≠ 0) in which an acidic hydroxy group has been replaced by an amino or substituted amino group.

nodes.label: sulfonamide
nodes.desc: An amide of a sulfonic acid RS(=O)<small><sub>2</sub></small>NR'<small><sub>2</sub></small>.

nodes.label: lipopeptide
nodes.desc: A compound consisting of a peptide with attached lipid.

nodes.label: lipid
nodes.desc: 'Lipids' is a loosely defined term for substances of biological origin that are soluble in nonpolar solvents. They consist of saponifiable lipids, such as glycerides (fats and oils) and phospholipids, as well as nonsaponifiable lipids, principally steroids.

nodes.label: primary amide
nodes.desc: A derivative of an oxoacid RkE(=O)l(OH)m (l ≠ 0) in which an acidic hydroxy group has been replaced by an amino or substituted amino group.

nodes.label: organosulfur compound
nodes.desc: An organosulfur compound is a compound containing at least one carbon-sulfur bond.

nodes.label: oxolanes
nodes.desc: Any oxacycle having an oxolane (tetrahydrofuran) skeleton.

nodes.label: secondary carboxamide
nodes.desc: A carboxamide resulting from the formal condensation of a carboxylic acid with a primary amine; formula RC(=O)NHR<small><sup>1</small></sup>.

nodes.label: pyrroline
nodes.desc: Any organic heteromonocyclic compound with a structure based on a dihydropyrrole.

nodes.label: diol
nodes.desc: A compound that contains two hydroxy groups, generally assumed to be, but not necessarily, alcoholic. Aliphatic diols are also called glycols.

nodes.label: enone
nodes.desc: An α,β-unsaturated ketone of general formula R<small><sup>1</small></sup>R<small><sup>2</small></sup>C=CR<small><sup>3</small></sup>‒C(=O)R<small><sup>4</small></sup> (R<small><sup>4</small></sup> ≠ H) in which the C=O function is conjugated to a C=C double bond at the α,β position.

nodes.label: polyol
nodes.desc: A compound that contains two or more hydroxy groups.

nodes.label: diazole
nodes.desc: An azole that is either one of a pair of heterocyclic organic compounds comprising three carbon atoms and two nitrogen atoms arranged in a ring.

nodes.label: alpha,beta-unsaturated ketone
nodes.desc: A ketone of general formula R<small><sup>1</small></sup>R<small><sup>2</small></sup>C=CR<small><sup>3</small></sup>‒C(=O)R<small><sup>4</small></sup> (R<small><sup>4</small></sup> ≠ H) or R<small><sup>1</small></sup>C≡C‒C(=O)R<small><sup>2</small></sup> (R<small><sup>2</small></sup> ≠ H) in which the ketonic C=O function is conjugated to an unsaturated C-C bond at the α,β position.

nodes.label: 1-(5-hydroxyhexyl)-3,7-dimethyl-3,7-dihydro-1H-purine-2,6-dione
nodes.desc: A dimethylxanthine that is 3,7-dihydro-1H-purine-2,6-dione which is substituted at positions 1,3 and 7 by a 5-hydroxyhexyl group, methyl group and methyl group, respectively.

nodes.label: drug
nodes.desc: Any substance which when absorbed into a living organism may modify one or more of its functions. The term is generally accepted for a substance taken for a therapeutic purpose, but is also commonly used for abused substances.

nodes.label: pharmaceutical
nodes.desc: Any substance introduced into a living organism with therapeutic or diagnostic purpose.

nodes.label: application
nodes.desc: Intended use of the molecular entity or part thereof by humans.

nodes.label: organic molecular entity
nodes.desc: Any molecular entity that contains carbon.

nodes.label: purines
nodes.desc: A class of imidazopyrimidines that consists of purine and its substituted derivatives.

nodes.label: carbonyl compound
nodes.desc: Any compound containing the carbonyl group, C=O. The term is commonly used in the restricted sense of aldehydes and ketones, although it actually includes carboxylic acids and derivatives.

nodes.label: organic acid
nodes.desc: Any organic molecular entity that is acidic and contains carbon in covalent linkage.

nodes.label: thiazoles
nodes.desc: An azole in which the five-membered heterocyclic aromatic skeleton contains a N atom and one S atom.

nodes.label: sodium salt
nodes.desc: Any alkali metal salt having sodium(1+) as the cation.

nodes.label: monohydroxyquinoline
nodes.desc: A hydroxyquinoline carrying a single hydroxy substituent.

nodes.label: quinolines
nodes.desc: A class of aromatic heterocyclic compounds each of which contains a benzene ring ortho fused to carbons 2 and 3 of a pyridine ring.

nodes.label: organooxygen compound
nodes.desc: An organochalcogen compound containing at least one carbon-oxygen bond.

nodes.label: tertiary alcohol
nodes.desc: A tertiary alcohol is a compound in which a hydroxy group, ‒OH, is attached to a saturated carbon atom which has three other carbon atoms attached to it.

nodes.label: ester
nodes.desc: A compound formally derived from an oxoacid RkE(=O)l(OH)m (l > 0) and an alcohol, phenol, heteroarenol, or enol by linking with formal loss of water from an acidic hydroxy group of the former and a hydroxy group of the latter.

nodes.label: phenylethanolamines
nodes.desc: An ethanolamine compound having a phenyl (substituted or unsubstituted) group on the carbon bearing the hydroxy substituent.

nodes.label: phenols
nodes.desc: Organic aromatic compounds having one or more hydroxy groups attached to a benzene or other arene ring.

nodes.label: organic hydroxy compound
nodes.desc: An organic compound having at least one hydroxy group attached to a carbon atom.

nodes.label: diester
nodes.desc: A diester is a compound containing two ester groups.

nodes.label: amino alcohol
nodes.desc: An alcohol containing an amino functional group in addition to the alcohol-defining hydroxy group.

nodes.label: methanesulfonates
nodes.desc: Esters or salts of methanesulfonic acid.

nodes.label: organosulfonate salt
nodes.desc: Any organic salt prepared using an organosulfonic acid as the acid component.

nodes.label: 11beta-hydroxy steroid
nodes.desc: Any 11-hydroxy steroid in which the hydroxy group at position 11 has β- configuration.

nodes.label: propanoate ester
nodes.desc: Any carboxylic ester where the carboxylic acid component is  propionic acid.

nodes.label: fluorinated steroid
nodes.desc: A steroid which is substituted with one or more fluorine atoms in any position.

nodes.label: corticosteroid
nodes.desc: A natural or synthetic analogue of the hormones secreted by the adrenal gland.

nodes.label: thioester
nodes.desc: A compound of general formula RC(=O)SR'. Compare with thionoester, RC(=S)OR'.

nodes.label: 3-oxo-Delta(1),Delta(4)-steroid
nodes.desc: A 3-oxo-Δ<small><sup>1</small></sup> steroid containing an additional double bond between positions 4 and 5.

nodes.label: steroid
nodes.desc: Any of naturally occurring compounds and synthetic analogues, based on the cyclopenta[a]phenanthrene carbon skeleton, partially or completely hydrogenated; there are usually methyl groups at C-10 and C-13, and often an alkyl group at C-17. By extension, one or more bond scissions, ring expansions and/or ring contractions of the skeleton may have occurred. Natural steroids are derived biogenetically from squalene which is a triterpene.

nodes.label: thiocarboxylic ester
nodes.desc: An ester in which one or both oxygens of an ester group have been replaced by divalent sulfur.

nodes.label: 3-oxo-Delta(1) steroid
nodes.desc: Any 3-oxo steroid that contains a double bond between positions 1 and 2.

nodes.label: 3-oxo-Delta(4) steroid
nodes.desc: A 3-oxo steroid conjugated to a C=C double bond at the α,β position.

nodes.label: dichlorobenzene
nodes.desc: Any member of the class of chlorobenzenes carrying two chloro groups at unspecified positions.

nodes.label: amino acid
nodes.desc: A carboxylic acid containing one or more amino groups.

nodes.label: indol-3-yl carboxylic acid
nodes.desc: Any indolyl carboxylic acid carrying an indol-3-yl or substituted indol-3-yl group.

nodes.label: N-acylindole
